title: MicroHop Sampling Scheduler + Provenance Digest Pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: smart routing (region selection, tier routing, fallback variants) produces long, chatty per-hop trace artifacts that are expensive to store and hard to query. We need a lightweight, replayable representation that preserves causal provenance for debugging policy decisions while limiting storage and privacy exposure.

Proposal: implement a MicroHop Sampling Scheduler that adaptively samples per-request hop frames and an enrichment stage that emits a compact Provenance Digest for every routed request. Provenance Digest = stable policy identifiers + hashed minimal context (prefix fingerprint, model variant id, tier id, region id, fallback_reason) + delta summary (latency, token delta, cost delta). Sampled micro-hop frames (raw artifacts) are stored only for a small percentage of requests with a TTL and pinned on demand. This balances debuggability with cost.

Goals:
- Make routing decisions explainable end-to-end with compact searchable artifacts.
- Keep baseline ingestion increase < 7% for 95th percentile traffic.
- Enable fast anomaly detection and RCA with digest-level joins before retrieving full frames.
- Per-tenant sampling controls and opt-out for sensitive customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Provenance Digest emitted for 100% of routed requests and visible in the routing-events index. 2) Digest contains stable policy ids, hashed prefix fingerprint, model_variant, region, tier, fallback_reason, latency_ms, token_delta, cost_delta. 3) Storage increase for telemetry pipeline < 7% at 95th percentile after default sampling. 4) Ability to request full micro-hop frame via console link (on sampled artifacts) and TTL of sampled frames enforced. 5) Security review completed and opt-out flag available to customers. 6) End-to-end test showing a simulated capacity fallback produces correct digest and a pinned frame retrievable by engineers.
technical_decisions:
- Use a deterministic 64-bit SipHash of normalized prefix and request context as the prefix_fingerprint to avoid storing raw prompt text.
- Provenance Digest is single-line JSON with pre-agreed compact keys (pd_v, pid, pf, mv, reg, tier, fb, lat, tokd, costd, ts).
- MicroHop Sampler runs as a lightweight filter in the routing layer, emitting both a digest to the telemetry topic and, when sampled, the full hop frame to the artifact store.
- Adaptive sampling: baseline rate 0.5% per tenant; increase to 5% on anomaly signals (error rate spike or SLO breach) using a token-bucket per-tenant scheduler.
- Feature flag gating and gradual rollout via console.
- All persisted sampled artifacts encrypted with customer KMS when tenant has Private deployment flag.
implementation_notes:
Work split into 3 sub-tasks: 1) Routing layer sampler + digest serializer (gRPC event) 2) Enrichment and digest schema registration + index mapping in telemetry (routing-events) 3) Artifact storage + console retrieval UI and access control.

Key files/PRs: RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/routing/microhop-digest-rfc, initial proto: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proto/pull/142, telemetry mapping PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/783.

Runbook knobs: per-tenant baseline_sampling_rate, anomaly_boost_multiplier, max_daily_artifacts. Default conservative config applied to all tenants.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged canary on internal tenants (5% traffic) for 3 days. 2) Monitor telemetry ingestion, storage, and latency; adjust baseline sampling. 3) Expand to +25% customers and run privacy review. 4) Full rollout with console controls and docs. 5) Post-rollout retrospective after two weeks.
migration_plan: Existing routing-event consumers should ignore unknown pd_v fields. We will publish a compatibility note; the enrichment stage will emit both legacy_route_event and provenance_digest for 4 weeks to allow downstream migration. After consumers confirm, legacy payload will be removed.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for digest canonicalization and hash stability.
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic that triggers region fallback and tier downgrade; assert digest fields match expected values.
- Load test: simulate 2x production QPS ensuring ingestion increase < 7%.
- Security test: verify no raw prompt text is stored in digest and sampled artifact encryption works.
monitoring_and_metrics:
- metric: routing.digest.emitted.count (per-tenant)
- metric: routing.microhop.sampled.count
- alert: telemetry.ingest.rate.delta > +10%
- dashboard: digest-latency-by-tier, sample-rate-by-tenant, artifact-retrieval-latency
- RCA helper: digest join query example: SELECT pid, mv, reg, fb, count(*) FROM routing-events WHERE time>... GROUP BY pid,mv,reg,fb
privacy_and_security_notes:
- Provenance Digest uses irreversible hashing for prefix_fingerprint and does not include raw prompt text.
- Customers can opt-out of sampling; Private deployments default to 0.02% baseline.
- Sampled artifacts are encrypted with tenant KMS where available; access logged.
docs_and_customer_communication:
- Console docs: how to interpret Provenance Digest fields, request full frame, and set sampling rates.
- Release note: short blurb about improved observability for routing decisions with privacy-preserving digests.
- Internal runbook: how to escalate when a digest indicates repeated fallback loops.
